div.head: V Atr 4.1
div.ab: ⁊ huruþinga Godes þeowas—biscopas ⁊ abbudas, munecas ⁊ mynecena, preostas ⁊ nunnan—to rihte gebugan ⁊ regollice libban ⁊ for eall Cristen folc þingian georne.
⁊ huruþinga Godes þeowas — biscopas ⁊ habbodas, munucas ⁊ mynecena, preostas ⁊ nunnan — to rihte gebugan ⁊ regollice libban ⁊ for eall Cristen folc þingian georne.
And huruþinga Godes þeowas — biscopas ⁊ abbodas, munecas ⁊ minicena, preostas ⁊ nunnan — to rihte gebugan ⁊ regollice libban ⁊ for eal Cristen folc geornlice þingian.
And huruþinga Godes þeowas—biscopas ⁊ abbodas, munecas ⁊ minicena, preostas ⁊ nunnan—to rihte gebugan ⁊ regollice libban ⁊ for eal Cristen folc geornlice þingian.
And huruþinga Godes þeowas—biscopas and abbudas, munecas and mynecena, preostas and nunnan—to rihte gebugan and regollice libban, and for eall Cristen folc þingian georne.

und vor allen Dingen sollen Gottesdiener — Bischöfe und Äbte, Mönche und Mönchinnen, Priester und Nonnen — der Rechtspflicht sich unterwerfen und nach [kanonischer] Regel leben und eifrig für alles Christenvolk Fürbitte thun.

and above all let the servants of God — bishops and abbots, monks and nuns [of a rule], priests and nuns — submit to their duty and live according to the [canonical] rule and pray eagerly for all Christian people.

and most of all the servants of God, bishops and abbots, monks and nuns, priests and women under religious vows, shall submit to their duty, and live according to their rule, and zealously intercede for all Christian people.

And especially God’s servants—bishops and abbots, monks and nuns, priests and women dedicated to God—are to submit to their duty and to live according to their rule and to intercede zealously for all Christian people.

And indeed, God’s servants—bishops and abbots, male and female monastics, priests and nuns—are to submit to their duty and live according to their rule, and fervently intercede for all Christian people.
div.note: Vgl. Ine 1 | Vgl. I Em. 1; IV Eg. 1, 7
Liebermann compares Ine 1; I Em 1; IV Eg 1.7.
female monastics: Old English mynecena, a special category of female monastic established during the Monastic Reform of the tenth century.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Nonne 1. Noch im 12. Jh. scheidet von sanctimonialis (Klosternonne) die nunna I Cn 7, 1 In. Männer dürfen nicht essen on mynecena beodderne; dahinter stellt als weniger streng gebunden preostas and nunnan Hom. n. Wulfstan ed. Napier 269

Cf. Gl Nonne 1. Even in the 12th cent. I Cn 7, 1 In distinguishes the nunna from the sanctimonialis (cloistered nun). Men may not eat on mynecena beodderne; after them, as less strictly bound, Hom. n. Wulfstan ed. Napier 269 places preostas and nunnan

Wie in voriger Z. entsprechen hier Priester den Nonnen im engeren (von Mönchinnen verschiedenen) Sinne. ‘Priester’ liest Hom. n. Wulfstan 269, der auch VI Atr 2. I Cn 6 benutzt. Dafür hat canonicas VI 2 = I Cn 6. Diese Stiftsgeistlichen aber erwähnt V 7 = VI 4 besonders. Vermutlich will der Änderer die Landpfarrer aus der Regel herauslassen

As in the preceding line, priests here correspond to nuns in the narrower sense (as distinct from cloistered nuns). ‘Priests’ is the reading of Hom. n. Wulfstan 269, which also uses VI Atr 2. I Cn 6. In its place VI 2 = I Cn 6 has canonicas. These collegiate clergy, however, are mentioned separately in V 7 = VI 4. Presumably the reviser wants to exempt the country parish priests from the rule
Regelwidrige will jener Homilet mit Friedlosigkeit und Landesverweisung strafen 269
That homilist would punish those who break the rule with outlawry and banishment 269
Cf. IV Edg. 1, 7; VI Atr. 2; 41; I Cn. 4, 3; Wulfstan, pp. 120, 179.
